The output-bound calculation now runs on the saved surrogate members. It checks each
export against JAX, bounds the output across the declared input box and splits that box
within an explicit budget. The results differ between the three surrogates.

| surrogate | result |
|---|---|
| EC | [all five EC members have finite CROWN bounds for both launcher families; current and width bounds remain very loose]{.claim}[C-262](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-262){.cid .st-measured} |
| pedestal | [all nine pedestal pressure and half-width pairs have finite bounds over the recorded ITER trajectory box, with the widening and domain clipping stated]{.claim}[C-263](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-263){.cid .st-measured} |
| transport | [all twenty members of each transport ensemble have finite training-space bounds that overflow the inverse signed-log transform; no finite physical guard domain is certified]{.claim}[C-264](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-264){.cid .st-measured} |

For EC, each launcher family keeps every other input range from the stored training box.
The serving clamps limit absorbed power, deposition centres and minimum widths. Bounds on
current and maximum width remain much broader than the outputs sampled inside the box.
Finite enclosure therefore does not yet mean a useful physical limit.

The old pedestal diagnostic saved its predictions but omitted the network inputs. The
updated diagnostic records those inputs and the model hash. A fresh run supplied the
visited span; the proof box widens it by a stated margin within the upstream domain.
All pressure and half-width solutions are retained, including the solution used by TORAX.
There is still no comparison with labelled EPED data.

For transport, the finite bounds in signed-log training space are so wide that the
inverse transform overflows. The reports retain those bounds and mark the physical result
unknown. This is a limitation of the bound calculation within its budget, not evidence
that the network reaches those extremes or a reason to change the acceptance limits.

Each split covers the original domain completely. Sampled extrema check enclosure and
measure tightness; they never substitute for proof. The audit binds the model, property,
source and evidence, and checks the retained partitions. Production guards still use their
existing contracts.

## What's next

Tighter transport bounds are needed before V5 can supply physical guard domains. The
remaining M4 work also includes local robustness, the EC coupled comparison, guard
integration and the owner's final certification review. MAST-U's accepted scope limitation
remains in force.
